subject: EdgeScale S3-backed vector adapter: onboarding checklist and kickoff
messages:
From: Lucas Moreno <lucas@edgescale.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: interest in S3-backed vector adapter (EdgeScale) -> kickoff

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking the call earlier — appreciated the fast follow. EdgeScale is excited to get started on the S3-backed vector adapter integration with Redwood. We sketched an initial scope on our side and want to validate a few technical items before the kickoff: 

1) S3 object layout: we currently assume vectors will be sharded into prefix buckets by customer-id/segment and stored as compressed parquet blobs. Any constraints or preferred key formats from Redwood's side?
2) Auth model: we plan to use short-lived signed URLs generated from a service role. Is there a preference for IRSA (AWS) or a Redwood-managed presign endpoint?
3) KV cache interaction: for hot-path reads, EdgeScale will consult a local LRU cache, then fallback to S3. Do you have specific expectations around cache invalidation hooks or Webhook events from Redwood when index versions roll?

Attached is our onboarding checklist (edge-adapter-onboarding-checklist.xlsx) and a minimal S3 permissions snippet (s3-permissions-snippet.txt). Can we target a kickoff next Tue 6/30 10:00 PT?

Best,
Lucas
Lucas Moreno
Integration Lead, EdgeScale

Subject: Re: EdgeScale S3-backed vector adapter: onboarding checklist and kickoff

Lucas — thanks for the checklist and clear questions. Good news: the proposed approach aligns with our expectations but a few clarifications so the kickoff is high bandwidth: 

- Object layout: Redwood prefers stable prefixing so our routing can map quickly to index shards. Use customer-id/segment/YYYYMMDD as the high-level prefix and include a small manifest.json per shard that lists vector-count and embedding-dim. We don't require parquet specifically; compressed NDJSON or parquet are both fine.
- Auth model: we strongly prefer short-lived signed URLs issued by the customer's deployment. For Redwood-hosted customers we can offer a presign endpoint but for Dedicated/Private we recommend IRSA/service-role. We'll go over options in the meeting.
- Cache invalidation: we have a webhook schema for index version events (index.rollout, index.purge). Ben, can you paste the webhook schema in a follow-up?

Kickoff: Tue 2026-06-30 10:00 PT works for us. We will invite Emily from Pinecone to discuss routing fallbacks. Agenda below:
1) Quick intros (5m)
2) Object layout & manifest example (10m)
3) Auth & presign patterns (10m)
4) Cache invalidation & rollout hooks (10m)
5) Acceptance criteria & timeline (15m)

See you on Tue. I've attached a short template for the manifest naming example.

-Irene
Irene Choi

Hey all — adding the webhook schema excerpt below for Lucas to consume prior to the call. Also included a short Ops checklist for test buckets.

--- webhook schema (excerpt) ---
Event: index.rollout
Payload: {"index_id": "string", "version": "string", "timestamp": "ISO8601"}
Delivery: POST JSON to partner endpoint with HMAC-SHA256 signature header X-Redwood-Signature
Retries: exponential backoff (3 attempts)

--- ops test-bucket checklist ---
- Create a dedicated test bucket with prefix redwood-poc/<partner-name>/
- Apply bucket policy to restrict access to test service role
- Enable server-side encryption (SSE-KMS)
- Add lifecycle rule to auto-delete objects older than 14 days

Lucas, attaching a minimal presign endpoint example and the HMAC signing snippet as s3-permissions-snippet.txt. If you want, we can seed a sample manifest and small dataset for you to validate reads before the meeting.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
